title: Choosing the Right LTO Partner Matters Now More Than Ever
summary: Surging electricity demand. Favorable economics. Paired LTO and uprates. These are just some of the compelling reasons Long-Term Operation programs are gaining momentum among U.S. utilities. As nuclear energy demand continues to grow, many utilities are turning to LTO to transform aging assets into expanded capacity.

title: NRC reviews first 100 days after reorganization
summary: Roughly 100 days ago, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission began a massive structural reorganization, which included, among other changes, a reorganization around core business lines and the establishment of two new offices: the Office of the Chief Nuclear Reactor Inspector and the Office of Advanced Reactors. On October 15, NRC officials and staff met with the five commissioners at the NRC Region IV offices in Arlington, Texas, to assess the successes and challenges resulting from the reorganization. Commissioners welcomed the chance to hold a meeting at a regional office, which allowed them to see firsthand how the changes are impacting staff not based at the NRC’s Maryland headquarters. One of the main changes to the reorganization is having all four regional offices report to the new CNRI.

title: Nuclear Industry Calls For Concrete Action In EU Post-2030 Energy Framework
summary: Senior executives from Europe’s nuclear industry have called on the European Commission to take “concrete steps” to support nuclear investments under the EU’s post-2030 energy and climate framework, including a common clean energy target covering both nuclear power and renewables. In a letter dated 19 October to European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, the executives urged the EU to move away from technology-specific targets and ensure that all low-carbon energy sources receive equal policy support.

title: Amazon, AEP, X-energy explore SMR feasibility in Indiana
summary: Amazon, American Electric Power, and X-energy are partnering up to potentially bring a 960-MW nuclear power plant to western Indiana as the state’s first commercial nuclear generation. The three announced earlier today a joint development agreement to explore the feasibility of a nuclear power project at the former Breed coal-fired power plant in Sullivan County, Ind., that would involve the deployment of 12 X-energy Xe-100 high-temperature, gas-cooled reactors. Details on the project are minimal outside of the reactor design and site, as it is in the early stages and has yet to reach any final investment decision. However, this project could create more than 1,000 construction jobs and more than 100 permanent jobs, the companies said.

title: Centrus Announces $116 Million Acquisition Of Centrifuge Component Supplier Westerman
summary: US nuclear fuel company Centrus Energy has acquired Westerman Holdings, a major supplier of components for its uranium enrichment centrifuges, for about $116m (€103m), a statement said. Centrus said the acquisition was financed through about $95m in cash and $21m in equity.

title: Slovakia’s Mochovce-4 Nuclear Power Plant Connected To Grid For First Time
summary: The Mochovce-4 nuclear power plant in Slovakia has been connected to the national electricity grid for the first time, marking a major milestone in the commissioning of the VVER-440 reactor unit. Slovak owner Slovenské Elektrárne said the first of the unit’s two turbine generators was synchronised with the grid at 20:41 local time on 15 October and began supplying electricity.
